name: DungeonSwap swap router pulls approved tokens for any caller-named user
summary: The unverified DungeonSwap router 0x544fde4e... exposes 0x4f1f05bc, which transferFroms the input token from a caller-supplied user address and swaps it along a caller-supplied path, sending the output to that user, with no check that the caller is the user or an authorised front end. Anyone could therefore spend every allowance granted to the router: attackers forced approved wallets' BUSD, USDT, USDC and other tokens into buys of DND or other tokens they then dumped. The first drain (29 wallets) came at block 26028397 and hundreds of copycat senders continued until October 2025.
notes: Immutable unverified router runtime; Etherscan txlist shows no transaction to it after creation (owner functions never called), so deployment supplies the age.

Lower bound on victim input across 11,251 unauthorised router calls in 7,308 transactions by 457 senders against 6,474 wallets (blocks 26028397..63995459). Stablecoin legs are counted at par: victim stablecoin inputs, or the stablecoin output of a victim-token first hop. WBNB legs are counted only for the first-day campaign (blocks up to 26040000: 63.467677718180654806 WBNB at the anchor-time quote); 116.66 WBNB of later WBNB legs and 1,776 first hops whose input and output are neither WBNB nor a stablecoin (e.g. CAKE, ETH, zSEED routed directly) are not valued. Victims received the path's output tokens (mostly DND) at manipulated prices; that output is not netted.
